The Longhorns are back on the cusp of the top 10 after a huge home win over Ole Miss this weekend

        Utah and Texas both took big jumps in the latest Associated Press top 25 poll after wins over top-15 opponents this weekend.   Utah, the lone remaining unbeaten team in the Big 12, moved all the way up to No. 6 after a 21-13 win over Houston Saturday night. The Utes were one of the biggest movers of the week after checking in at No. 10 last week.  So, too, was Texas which jumped from No. 19 to No. 11 after its 34-27 win over Ole Miss. The Rebels dropped to No. 12 from No. 7 following the loss to the Longhorns.   BYU's time in the top three was short lived. The Cougars, who moved all the way up to No. 2 after a win over Notre Dame last week, fell down to No. 8 after a double-overtime loss to unranked Central Florida.   
Texas Tech also experienced a big drop down to No. 13 following its loss to Cincinnati.   AP pollRankTeamPoints1Miami (FL) 7-01,735 (59)2Ohio State 6-11,681 (10)3Georgia 6-11,5114Indiana 7-11,4595Notre Dame 6-11,4586Utah 7-01,413 (1)7UCLA 7-01,3988BYU 6-11,3259Kentucky 7-11,18510Alabama 6-21,06311Texas 5-296612Ole Miss 5-287113Texas Tech 6-186114Wake Forest 6-182215LSU 6-281316Tennessee 6-266217Florida 5-255618Houston 6-249119SMU 6-144020Boise State 6-142220Northwestern 6-142222Arizona 6-140023Missouri 5-232924Oklahoma State 5-218025Wisconsin 5-2125Others receiving votes: Iowa 76, New Mexico 41, Cincinnati 11, Oregon State 10, South Carolina 8, Minnesota 7, USC 7, UTSA 1, Virginia Tech 1The SEC is a battlegroundGeorgia remains the SEC's highest-ranked team at No. 3, but chaos again reared its head within the conference. The SEC's next two highest-ranked teams from a week ago -- No. 7 Ole Miss and No. 11 Tennessee -- both lost Saturday. No. 9 Kentucky and No. 10 Alabama moved into the top 10 after those losses, but it's clear the College Football Playoff selection committee will have an awfully hard time assessing the SEC's top teams.The SEC has four teams ranked Nos. 9-12, including the Wildcats, who are ranked one spot ahead of a team they lost to earlier this season. The calendar hasn't even turned to November, yet there are no undefeated SEC teams and only two remaining one-loss teams in Kentucky and Georgia. Prepare for a glut of three-loss SEC teams, all with their own strengths and weaknesses.Props to WisconsinEntering this season, CBS Sports experts voted on which coaches were on the hottest seats and came up with a top four of Baylor's Dave Aranda, Florida State's Mike Norvell, Maryland's Mike Locksley and Wisconsin's Luke Fickell. Aranda and Locksley have since been fired, while Norvell sits on the hottest seat in college football.Fickell? He has a top-25 team now after a win over USC on Saturday. It's Wisconsin's first appearance in the AP Top 25 since September 2023. Wisconsin's decision to invest more in its roster and give Fickell one more shot has paid off in 2026 thus far. The Badgers are 5-2, with additional wins over Penn State and Michigan State.With a manageable schedule that includes games against Maryland, Rutgers and Purdue, there's a very real chance Fickell could lead the Badgers to eight or nine wins this season.

        With one week left until the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, no team is safe from the chaos. That is reflected in the spreads for some of Week 9's biggest matchups.One of the bigger spreads in top-25 matchups is Georgia going to Atlanta as a two-score favorite against Florida. The Bulldogs entered their open date on a low note with a devastating loss to Auburn, but the Gators were riding high on the heels of a top-10 win over Texas in Austin.With Julian Sayin sidlined by an injury, Ohio State goes into Los Angeles to take on a mentally wounded USC team, which just fell to unranked Wisconsin. In spite of their big question at quarterback, the Buckeyes opened as favorites against the Trojans.There are just three unbeaten teams remaining in college football -- Miami, Utah and UCLA. The Hurricanes and Bruins are massive favorites in Week 9, but the Utes face a tricky road trip to Cincinnati.
Let's take a look at the schedule and early lines.Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.The big gamesFlorida vs. Georgia (-10.5): This is technically a neutral-site game, although the crowd at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta will probably lean red-and-black. Both teams are coming off an open date, but the way each entered the off week couldn't be more different. Florida went into Austin with its backup quarterback and rallied for a comeback win over No. 7 Texas. Georgia suffered a stunning upset at the hands of rival Auburn, knocking the Bulldogs from their spot atop atop the rankings. Despite that, the oddsmakers see the Dawgs as an obvious favorite.Ohio State (-7) at USC: It doesn't necessarily reflect well upon Lincoln Riley that Ohio State is a touchdown favorite in Los Angeles despite starting a backup quarterback. It's not hard to see why this line is what it is after watching the Trojans struggle to move the ball against Wisconsin in a 24-7 loss to the Badgers on Saturday night. Star quarterback Jayden Maiava looked pedestrian, and while the USC defense played well enough to win, Wisconsin doesn't have anyone remotely like Heisman Trophy favorite Jeremiah Smith on their roster.Arizona at Texas Tech (-4.5): The Wildcats have very quietly rolled to a 6-1 start, and their lone loss was an 11-point defeat in Provo. Now, they will faced a frustrated Texas Tech team in Lubbock. The Red Raiders got beaten rather convincingly by Cincinnati, 37-24, in Week 8. Will Hammond continues to struggle at quarterback. Super booster Cody Campbell is tweeting about it being an inxecusable loss. If Texas Tech can't regroup and pull itself together, Arizona is more than capable of handing the Red Raiders their second straight loss. The winner's Big 12 and College Football Playoff chances will get a nice boost.
Wisconsin at Iowa (-3.5): After losing the battle for the Floyd of Rosedale -- a 98-pound bronze pig -- Iowa will get an immediate shot at redemption this week. The Hawkeyes and Badgers will play for the Heartland Trophy, a 72-pound brass bull. Which trophy is more prestigious? Your answer depends on your preference between pork and beef. While Iowa just suffered a heartbreaking last-minute loss to Minnesota, Wisconsin is riding high after picking up a top-25 win over USC, and the Badgers are 3-1 in Big Ten play.Minnesota at Indiana (-20.5): Despite Minnesota's win over Iowa and Indiana's struggles against Michigan, the oddsmakers don't have much faith in the Golden Gophers. To be fair, Minnesota hasn't given anyone much reason to trust it this fall with a 25-point loss to Mississippi State and a 28-point loss to Purdue on its resume. Still, the Hoosiers haven't made life easy on themselves lately. They needed overtime to beat a Michigan team that was starting freshman Tommy Carr at quarterback, and Josh Hoover threw for just 81 yards.Utah (-6.5) at Cincinnati: One week after handing Texas Tech its first loss of the season, Cincinnati has the chance to take down another unbeaten Big 12 opponent. The Bearcats rode their running game and an opportunistic defense to a win in Nippert Stadium on Saturday, but can they do that twice in a row? The Utes are coming off a hard-fought top-25 win over Houston late Saturday night, and it makes you wonder whether they could be the next team victimized the dreaded road trip immediately following an emotional win. Vegas certainly doesn't think Utah will roll into Cincinnati and run away with this game.

body:
The first-year offensive coordinator lasted just eight games before his firing

    12:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oregon has fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer after just seven games, the school announced Sunday. Dan Lanning promoted Mehringer following Will Stein's departure in the offseason, and that move has been roundly criticized, with the Ducks flailing on offense all year."Drew has been a valued member of this staff since 2022, and I am appreciative of everything he's done for Oregon," Lanning said in a statement. "He played a tremendous role in what this program has accomplished over the last several seasons. This was a decision I felt was in the best interest of our football program, as I believe a new direction is necessary to move our offense forward. I thank Drew for his efforts and wish him all the best."Last season, the Ducks ranked 11th nationally with 36.9 points per game, but that production dropped significantly under Mehringer's playcalling. Oregon has averaged 33.1 points per game this fall, and that number is inflated by an 84-0 win over Portland State.In Big Ten play, the Ducks have topped 17 points just once -- a 41-27 win over USC in which quarterback Dante Moore exited with a concussion that has sidelined him for the last three games. With Moore out of the lineup, Oregon has averaged 14 points per game.
Moore's injury is responsible for some of those offensive woes, but not all of them. The Ducks seemed to have one of the best backup quarterback situations in the country with Dylan Raiola transferring in from Nebraska, but he cost the team a win against UCLA and failed to do much of anything in a 21-10 loss to Illinois on Sunday.Oregon's offensive performance against the Illini was the final straw for Mehringer because -- even with the team down a few key offensive pieces -- it should have been able to put points on the board. Illinois ranks 16th in the Big Ten in yards allowed per game (382.4) and 17th in passing yards allowed per game (248.0).Lanning's decision to promote Mehringer from co-offensive coordinator doesn't look any better with Will Stein leading Kentucky to a 7-1 start in his first year on the job. The Wildcats are averaging 32.9 points per game with considerably fewer resources than the Ducks.

        Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is making his return this week against the Carolina Panthers, after missing the last three games with a right thumb injury. And to make his return to action a little easier, he got an assist from a World Series team. Mayfield will wear a custom glove to help protect his throwing thumb, given to him by the Tampa Bay Rays training staff. The Buccaneers reached out to Nike, which made a custom protective glove for MLB star Mike Trout. The inquiry led the Rays, who are playing in the 2026 World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, to offer to help.The Rays sent a member of the equipment staff to the Bucs' facility to meet with Mayfield and make the glove for him. According to the Tampa Bay Times, clubhouse attendant Nick Bond modified a wide receiver glove by removing material around the thumb and adding an insert for protection. Two gloves were made: one with hard plastic and another resembling a soft cast.
Here is a look at the glove:
"[It's] not restricting because it's on the backside. ... For me, just getting used to it. I don't feel the difference. It's just like me wearing a glove," Mayfield said. Rays equipment manager Tyler Wall spoke to the abilities of Bond and their plan for the glove. "I said our guy can do anything," Wall said. "They worked together and kind of Frankensteined a glove together, working with their trainers, Baker and Nick Bond. [It's] not hard enough to restrict the thumb but enough for protection. So he built a pocket around the thumb and inserted it. It worked pretty good."
The Rays are currently down 2-0 against the Brewers, but even as they prepared for this weekend's games, they were able to extend some help to another Tampa team.The Buccaneers sit at 1-5 on the season, losing two of the three games Mayfield missed. But their poor record is not all because of Mayfield's absence. Even when he was playing, Mayfield was struggling, with 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. The season's hope isn't over quite yet, thanks to the rest of the NFC South struggling as well.The Panthers, who Mayfield played for in 2022, lead the division at 3-2, followed by the 2-4 Atlanta Falcons and 2-4 New Orleans Saints.

title: 2026 World Series: How Rays can overcome 2-0 deficit to beat Brewers - CBS Sports
description: They have been two edge-of-your-seat wins, but the Milwaukee Brewers are up 2-0 over the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, and they're
body:
They have been two edge-of-your-seat wins, but the Milwaukee Brewers are up 2-0 over the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, and they're two wins away from the first championship in franchise history. Historically, teams with a 2-0 lead in a best-of-seven have gone on to win the series 83% of the time. The Brewers are in the driver's seat, but they know the job is not done, or even close to it."Their team is good." Brewers manager Pat Murphy said after Game 2. "They're the best team in the American League and I'm well aware of it. I think we had a lot of things go our way, and I realize that.  I respect Tampa, and we've got a long way to go."The series now shifts to Tropicana Field and the Rays will try to erase the 2-0 deficit, something that hasn't been done in the World Series in 30 years. Good news, though: You only need to look back to last season for the last time a team came back from down 2-0 in a best-of-seven. It is rare, but it is hardly unprecedented, and these Rays are plenty capable of it.In 95 tries, 16 teams have come back from a 2-0 deficit in a best-of-seven series. Six of the 16 occurred before 1980, and three occurred in 1985 alone. Here are the six 2-0 comebacks in the last 40 years:
SeriesWinnerLoserGames2025 ALCSBlue JaysMariners72023 NLCSDiamondbacksPhillies72020 NLCSDodgersBraves72004 ALCSRed SoxYankees71996 World SeriesYankeesBraves61986 World SeriesMetsRed Sox7The last two 2-0 comebacks in the World Series came in the sixth year of the decade. A good omen for the Rays? They'd better hope so. Tampa needs all the help it can get to beat the Brewers four times in the next five games. Note that those 2004 Red Sox are, of course, the only team in history to erase a 3-0 series deficit. A Game 3 win is an absolute must for the Rays.The Brewers last lost four times in five games from Aug. 10-14 during a West Coast trip through San Diego and Chavez Ravine. They lost four times in five games from July 8-12 as well, also on the road. That was a trip through St. Louis and Pittsburgh. The Brewers had six- and four-game losing streaks in April. A Rays comeback is improbable, not impossible.Here now is what needs to happen for the Rays to make that improbable comeback and win the World Series.1. Clean up the sloppy playThe Rays are usually the team that forces their opponent into sloppy play, and to be sure, the Brewers have played far from clean in the World Series. David Hamilton got thrown out at third trying to stretch a double into a triple in Game 1. Cooper Pratt spiked a throw to begin Game 1, which opened the door for Tampa's four-run inning. It hasn't been a crisp two games.The Rays, though, have shot themselves in the foot over and over again. Most egregiously, Jonathan Aranda dropped a foul popup in the first inning of Game 1, giving William Contreras new life. Contreras then singled as part of the two-run inning. Later in the game, Aranda let a ground ball get through his legs, Bill Buckner style. That led to Milwaukee's third run of the game.
There have been other mistakes throughout the World Series and the Rays simply can not give the Brewers extra outs, an extra 90 feet, and extra baserunners. The Brewers have made the Rays pay for their mistakes time and time again. It's baseball; mistakes happen, but Tampa will need to at least limit them moving forward, or ideally eliminate them entirely.  "We didn't play our cleanest baseball game by any stretch," Rays manager Kevin Cash said after Game 2. "We pride ourselves on doing everything we can to support the pitchers and making plays behind them.  Today was probably not our best day." 
        
            
                The Rays are making too many mistakes to stand a chance against the relentless Brewers
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
2. Get a great start from Freddy PeraltaThose 2-0 comebacks listed above have one thing in common: The starting pitcher was great in Game 3. Last year, Shane Bieber allowed two runs in six innings to spark Toronto's comeback. In 2023, Brandon Pfaadt fired 5 ⅔ shutout innings for the D-backs. In the 1996 World Series, it was David Cone for the Yankees. In the 1986 World Series, it was Bob Ojeda for the Mets.Freddy Peralta, the ALCS MVP and a former Brewer, will be charged with giving the Rays that great start in Game 3. He's been sensational this postseason, allowing just two runs in 16 ⅔ innings across three starts and one relief appearance. He's been great with the Rays in general. Since Aug. 26, Peralta, acquired from the Mets at the trade deadline, has a 0.88 ERA in nine starts, one relief appearance, and 50 ⅔ innings.
"I give Freddy a lot of credit for being a good pitcher and being vulnerable enough to say, 'I wasn't comfortable doing some things and I want to get back to my strengths,'" Cash said prior to the World Series. "He guided that through the entire two months he's been with us, and he took off in September and has continued to take off in October."If the Rays are going to make this a series, it has to start with Peralta. He must pitch well and also pitch deep into Game 3, because the middle of Tampa's bullpen is sketchy. Two games into the series, it feels like the Rays simply do not have enough arms to beat the Brewers. One game at a time, though. Peralta will start Game 3 and must pitch well to make a comeback possible.3. Enjoy some home cookingMost teams are better at home than on the road and there are a million reasons for that. The roster is tailored to their home ballpark. The players have better equipment and facilities available to them (the Trajekt hitting machine doesn't travel, for instance). They get to sleep in their own beds. They have their fans behind them. On and on we can go.The Rays are no different. At 55-26, they tied the Brewers (who else?) for baseball's best home record during the regular season. The Rays are uniquely built for Tropicana Field's bouncy turf. The turf plays very fast, so Tampa's hitters, by and large, put the ball on the ground and run like crazy. That is their home-field advantage. They use the turf expertly.Now, the flip side to this is that the Brewers had baseball's second-best road record during the regular season. They went 48-33 away from American Family Field, one game worse than the Dodgers and their MLB-best 49-32 road mark. If there is a team that won't cower at the Trop, it is these Brewers.RecordRun differentialRays at home55-26+51Rays on the road43-38+35RecordRun differentialBrewers at home55-26+166Brewers at home48-33+48The run differential tells the story. The Brewers are a juggernaut at home and merely very good on the road. They're a great team, no matter where they play, really. The Rays can take solace in the fact that the series now moves to Tampa and they will get to play Games 3, 4, and, if necessary, 5 on their literal home turf. If they're going to make a comeback, it starts at home."I know our fans are going to be really loud and excited to see us come back and kind of reset ourselves a little bit," Cash said after Game 2. "We've got a really good pitcher going, as do they. A lot of confidence in this club to respond. They've done it all season long, and they'll continue to do it."4. Get a little luckyWith their backs up against the wall, the Rays need every little break. A borderline pitch in a big spot (and the ABS challenge!) going their way. A bloop off the end of the bat landing just fair (or foul). A good defender booting a play. Something like that. It is better to be lucky than good, but to beat the Brewers four times in the next five games, the Rays will need to be lucky and good.

Hoover scored the eventual game-winning touchdown on a 4-yard run in the extra session, but his performance left much to be desired."There were a lot of discussions about (backup quarterback) Grant Wilson and Josh Hoover in the second half because Grant had a good week of practice and is really capable," Cignetti said. "At the end of the day, it's been Josh's season, and even though he's not 100%, we've got to finish it out with him, and he responded."
Hoover helped the Hoosiers avoid losing two straight for the first time in three years under Cignetti, and he was playing through injury after completing just one pass over Indiana's final five possessions -- a 21-yard hookup with tight end Brock Schott in overtime."I had to battle through some things this week to get out here," Hoover said. "I knew I was going to find a way to get out here and find a way to win this game for this team regardless of how I felt. There's guys on this team that are banged up every week. It's no different for me."Indiana's not the only top-10 team with quarterback concerns right now. Ohio State lost Julian Sayin for the foreseeable future after last week's win over the Hoosiers; unbeaten UCLA is without Nico Iamaleava, and Texas Tech's on-again, off-again Will Hammond hasn't enjoyed a multi-touchdown passing effort all season.
The Hoosiers looked gun-shy in the passing game throughout the second half as they nursed a narrow lead and did everything they could to avoid giving Michigan's anemic offense short-field scoring opportunities.Cignetti's not panicking after his team improved to 7-1 and remained very much in control of their CFP quest, but pretending all is well for the Hoosiers offensively after a couple of one-possession wins over Northwestern and Nebraska, with Minnesota and USC looming, is a problem."It's a great win," Cignetti said. "They come in all different shapes and sizes. Defense just kept them out of the end zone for the most part. Kept coming up with plays. Offense struggled to say the least. And yes, Josh Hoover did practice every day, but was limited a little bit, and we feel he'll get better and better every day physically.
"Who would have ever thought we'd run Josh down there for touchdowns? So the element of surprise is still alive in college football. Our defense backs the ball all the time, and came through, you know, a number of times, and it's a great win."Indiana's offensive strugglesHoover was handpicked by Cignetti and Indiana's offensive staff this portal cycle to be the replacement for Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza, who so often bailed the Hoosiers out of difficult situations last fall during an unbeaten run to hardware.However, production is down offensively across all categories, and that's going to be a problem the rest of the way and potentially in the playoff for the Hoosiers against elite competition.

body:
The 2026-27 college football coaching carousel is in full swing, and these teams will have to pony up to pay off their former coaches
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Baylor became the third Power Four program to fire its head coach on Sunday when it dismissed Dave Aranda after seven seasons. Baylor joined North Carolina State and Maryland as the coaching carousel finally got spinning in late October. With each firing comes a high financial cost to move on from the coach. What is each school paying to fire its coach, and where could it go next? CBS Sports breaks it down below.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    BaylorFired coach: Dave Aranda (40-40 in 7 seasons)Cost: Reportedly $12 millionBaylor fired Dave Aranda on Sunday following disappointing losses to TCU and Kansas. Aranda had seemingly cooled his seat with a 4-1 start, but those losses ultimately doomed him. As a private school, Baylor does not release coaching contracts the way public schools must. The buyout figure was believed to be approximately $12 million last season, while Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger reported that same figure for this year's cost. Candidates to replace Aranda include Boise State's Spencer Danielson and UTSA's Jeff Traylor. Check out the full list of Baylor coaching options here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MarylandFired coach: Mike Locksley (39-54 in 8 seasons)
Cost: $9.75 million Maryland kicked off the coaching carousel when it fired Mike Locksley on Wednesday. The school owes Locksley around $9.75 million with no offsets if he takes another job. Half of that $9.75 million is due to Locksley within sixty days. He had been under contract through 2028 but was let go after a 2-5 start to the season, which included losses to Rutgers, Virginia Tech and UCLA. Candidates to replace Locksley include Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, New Mexico's Jason Eck and Memphis' Charles Huff. Full candidates list here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    North Carolina StateFired coach: Dave Doeren (98-73 in 14 seasons)Cost: $10.3 million NC State opted for a rare Saturday afternoon firing when it dumped Dave Doeren after 14 seasons. There had been rumblings before the season that this could be Doeren's last in Raleigh, but that was centered around a possible retirement and not a firing. Instead, NC State will pay approximately $10.3 million to buy out the remainder of a contract set to run through 2029. NC State owes Doeren a little more than $600,000 within the next 30 days, and can then pay the remainder in monthly installments. The 54-year-old Doeren does have a clause in his contract requiring him to make reasonable efforts to find another job, which could offset the buyout NC State owes. 
The early candidate to watch to replace Doeren is former NC State quarterback great Philip Rivers. More on Rivers and NC State here.
